We appreciate the rapid turnaround — ValorBank is prioritizing this. Let us know if you need a shared dropbox or other access.

Subject: Preliminary evidence note: log/hash comparison and cache review

Priya / Alex / Connor —

Preliminary findings from our automated and manual checks for the 02:15–02:45 UTC window you flagged:

What we checked
- Full authn/authz logs (request metadata, response codes) across the serving fleet (all regions).
- Inference runtime access logs (model server read/write ops).
- Object-store access logs for any storage PUT/GETs initiated by inference nodes.
- Network egress logs and flow records for the time window.
- KV/prefix cache inspections and ephemeral cache sweep logs.

Methodology
- We produced a time-bound snapshot of all relevant logs and computed SHA-256 hashes for every log line.
- Hashes were signed with our incident key (HSM-backed) and the signature file is included in the chain_of_custody_signature.txt attachment.
- We compared the computed hashes to our standing snapshot taken 24 hours prior to the incident to detect insertion/modification.
- We executed a high-confidence sample review of request payloads where retention policy permitted (redacted when necessary) and reconstructed request paths.

Key results (preliminary)
- Total log lines examined: 1,248,912 (authn/authz + runtime + object store) across the time window.
- No log entries were present indicating outbound connections to unknown external hosts during the flagged interval. Network flow logs show egress only to our documented cloud providers and internal telemetry collectors.
- Object store access patterns in the window align with expected service operations; no bulk reads or enumerations of customer blobs were observed.
- KV/prefix cache sweeps show ephemeral cache flush at 02:42 UTC as scheduled; no entries persisted beyond retention thresholds.
- Hash comparison: 100% of hashes matched the pre-incident snapshot or were accounted-for by known retry events; no tamper detected.

Attachments included: log_hash_samples.csv (redacted examples of hashed lines), audit_scan_summary.pdf (full scan summary with timestamps and methodology), chain_of_custody_signature.txt (signed hash manifest).

Preliminary conclusion: at this stage we have found no evidence that any customer-record-level data was read and transmitted to an external destination. We will continue a complete forensics pass (including deep packet capture review for affected nodes) and will follow up with any new findings. Expected final confirmation: 2027-09-10 EOD PST.

Open asks for ValorBank
- If you have granular identifiers (trace ids or request ids) from your side, please share them — we can correlate to our internal traces to raise confidence.
- Preferred destination for the signed artifact bundle (S3 with pre-signed URL or shared Drive link)? We have a protected Drive ready: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/ValorBank-Incident-DFIR-20270908

— Marissa Cole
DFIR Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Final confirmation and evidence package — no customer data exposure identified

Priya / Valor security team —

Attached is the signed evidence package from our DFIR (see attachments and the Drive link below). Summary of final findings:

What we validated
- Complete log reconciliation across the serving fleet for 02:00–03:00 UTC.
- SHA-256 hash manifest signed by Redwood's incident HSM key (chain_of_custody_signature.txt).
- Network flow analysis showing no outbound connections to non-standard destinations correlated with any of the flagged requests.
- Object-store access review showing no bulk-download activity or enumeration that would indicate mass exfiltration.
- Ephemeral cache analysis confirming proper flush behavior; no cached payloads were present after scheduled sweeps.

Bottom line
- After processing ~3.2M lines of telemetry and performing the signed hash comparison, we found no evidence that ValorBank customer records were accessed by an external actor or exfiltrated as part of this incident.
- The anomalies you observed (500s) were correlated to an autoscaler race that caused transient errors and retry storms for a subset of requests; retries explain the unexpected patterns in your exported audit CSV. We have issued a runtime patch to harden autoscaler backoff behavior.

What we're handing over
- audit_scan_summary.pdf — detailed methodology, timestamps, node-ids, and itemized checks.
- log_hash_samples.csv — redacted examples and the hash manifest index.
- chain_of_custody_signature.txt — HSM-backed signature over the manifest.
- Drive bundle (read-only): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/ValorBank-Incident-DFIR-20270908

Next steps / offer
- If ValorBank would like, we can produce a signed attestation letter suitable for your audit team (SOC2 support) and a short review call to walk through the artifacts.
- If you provide request ids or trace ids from your logs, we will correlate them at the row level and include that mapping in an addendum.

Please reply to confirm receipt and whether you want the signed attestation letter. We can route the attestation through our legal team and provide an executed PDF within 48 hours.

Thanks again for the collaboration — let me know if you want a 30-min review this week.

— Alex Martinez
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
